title: Drain the water off a pan of dumplings into the sink, keeping every dumpling in the pan
instruction: Drain the water from the pan into the sink but keep all the dumplings in the pan, then set the pan back on the stove.
context: Draining pasta, potatoes or dumplings by holding the lid ajar is an everyday kitchen move: one hand tips the pan, the other holds the lid just open enough to let the water out and keep the food in. A lid that is not held slides off as the pan tips, and the food goes into the sink with the water.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A fixed dark grey stove block, 10 cm across and 13 cm tall, centred 27 cm forward and 1 cm right of the centre line. (2) On it, centred, a loose steel saucepan, inside 11 cm across and 7.5 cm deep, with a 3 mm wall and a 5 mm floor, 0.40 kg; its black handle, a bar 7 cm long, 2.5 cm wide and 2.2 cm tall, points straight back toward the arms from just under the rim. (3) Its lid, loose and centred on the rim: a flat steel disc 13.6 cm across (it overhangs the rim by 1 cm all round) and 4 mm thick, with no rim or skirt, and on top a black square knob 2.2 cm front to back, 3 cm side to side and 5.2 cm tall; 0.08 kg. (4) In the pan, six pale yellow dumplings (balls 24 mm across, 8 g each) in a ring on the floor, and the water: 20 blue beads 5 mm across, 0.5 g each. (5) A fixed white sink basin in front of the stove, inside 16 cm square and 7 cm deep, centred 41 cm forward and 1 cm right of the centre line. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot. In a real trial the pan holds 300 ml of tap water and six cooked potato gnocchi or mini dumplings about 2.5 cm across (about 8 g each); each simulated water bead stands for 15 ml of it.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. 0.0 unless the pan ends standing on the stove (tilted less than 10 degrees, its centre within 4 cm of the stove's). Otherwise 1.0 with at least 240 ml of the 300 ml drained into the sink (in the simulation at least 16 of the 20 water beads in the sink) and all 6 dumplings in the pan; 0.5 with at least 150 ml drained (10 beads) and at least 5 dumplings in the pan; 0.25 with at least 75 ml drained (5 beads) and all 6 dumplings in the pan; else 0.0. In a real trial the water drained is measured by weighing the pan with its contents before and after (1 g per ml), or by pouring what is left in the pan into a measuring jug, and the dumplings are counted in the pan. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held with the pan and every bead still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Refill the pan with 300 ml of water (in simulation: put the 20 water beads back), put the six dumplings back, stand the pan on the stove with its handle pointing back, centre the lid on it and dry the sink.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the 300 ml of water is 20 rigid 5 mm beads (15 ml each) that roll and pour but do not flow, splash or cling; the dumplings are rigid 24 mm balls; the pan's wall is 28 flat panels; the lid is a plain disc with no seal; nothing is hot. A real trial uses water and dumplings and measures the drained volume.
